reader.requirement: INTEGER-OF-DATE returns the number of days the valid Gregorian date YYYYMMDD (year above 1600, no upper bound at 1985) succeeds 1600-12-31.

edition-consulted.switches: the catalog's D8 edition window (IntroducedIn 85 for the 1989 module rows): the function is admitted at --std 85
DialectBehaviors.IsActive(IntegerDateFormBounded, year): inactive at 85, so BoundIntrinsicCall.IntegerDateFormUnbounded is true
renders `unbounded: true` into the CobolDate call when IntegerDateFormUnbounded

reader.edition-search: grep of IntrinsicBinder, IntrinsicRenderer, CobolDate and DialectBehavior for Edition, DialectLevel, DialectBehavior, IntegerDateForm, ConstructRegistry
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 INTEGER-OF-DATE(100000101) = 3,067,672; from 2002 a year past 9999 is an incorrect value (0)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers 1601-01-01, 9999-12-31 and the leap branches with literals; not a year past 9999 (the 1985 arm) or data-item arguments

probes.expected: proleptic Gregorian count with 1601-01-01 = day 1, every value checked against Python datetime; year 10000 representable at 1985 (the 1989 module bounds the year below only, §1989:A.2.16.3 AR1)
1985 admits years past 9999; 2002 and later end the integer date form at 3,067,671

reader.notes: DaysBeforeYear + DaysBefore + day; 1969-12-31 = 134774, 2024-03-01 = 154558 and 9999-12-31 = 3067671 match Python date arithmetic, and 10000-01-01 = 3067672 at 85. An invalid date (99999999) returns 0, within 1989's undefined result.

refuter.evidence: §1989:A.2.16.3 AR1: YYYY an integer greater than 1600 (no upper bound), MM 1..12, DD valid for the month and year; an invalid date is undefined (A.2.2).
